ceiling_directive: Execute the prescribed Xi0/Xi1 protocol and release a machine-checkable certificate proving positive uniform graph, injectivity, Jacobian, tail, and contrast-precision bounds with N_req <= 200000.
improvement_directive: Run the finite certifier on Xi0 and, only if required, Xi1, then supply the complete proof object with certified wrong-graph separation, remote and local injectivity, uniform Jacobian margins, controlled tails, and useful contrast precision.
critique: The note proves the full-column-rank injectivity frontier and stability bound, then transfers recovered laws to DAGs using Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin, but the central inversion is a direct log-PGF argument and the converse a simple Poisson nullspace construction, making the identification headline largely a composition of established ingredients. The finite-grid result is existential, while the elaborate tri-valued certifier has no delivered certified run: the Xi0/Xi1 separation, tail, uniform Jacobian, and N_req bounds remain precisely the open three-node benchmark. Consequently, the Wald theorem is conditional on certification without any nonvacuous prescribed design or reproducible certificate demonstrating useful precision. The framing discloses this limitation accurately, but the claimed bridge to a prospective empirical workflow lacks the delivered evidence needed for a field-tier or leading-journal contribution.
